Title: Trading wind generation from short-term probabilistic forecasts of wind power
Research_Question: How should wind power producers bid in electricity markets under asymmetric imbalance penalties using probabilistic forecasts?
Main_Contribution: Derives the analytical connection between asymmetric linear loss, optimal bidding quantile q = 1/(1+r), and market value.
Dataset_Scale: Operational Danish wind farm time series (Klim wind farm, multi-month SCADA, hourly spot and regulating market prices).
Experimental_Design: Evaluation of point forecasts vs probabilistic quantile bidding across varying penalty ratios r.
Operational_Metric: Market revenue, imbalance penalties, asymmetric linear loss.
Market_Formulation: Two-settlement day-ahead spot market plus dual-price imbalance cashout.
Introduction_Structure: Market background -> economic risk of point forecasts -> decision-theoretic framing -> paper roadmap.
Contribution_Paragraph_Structure: Numbered list of mathematical derivations and empirical verification.
Result_Section_Organization: Theoretical optimality curves -> empirical market settlement simulations -> sensitivity to penalty ratio.
Discussion_Style: Analytical and market-mechanism grounded, contrasting symmetric point loss with asymmetric trading regret.
Limitation_Style: Assumes price-taker status; notes price forecasting uncertainty as an unmodeled factor.
Table_Design: Clean single-column summary of revenue gains and penalty reductions under calibrated quantiles.
Figure_Design: Analytic cost curve vs quantile; empirical cumulative profit curves.
Claim_Strength: Level 3 (analytical proof of quantile optimality under linear loss + empirical backtesting).
How_Causal_Language_Controlled: Strictly uses mathematical derivation for optimality; uses backtest observations for market gains.
How_Novelty_Positioned: First rigorous decision-theoretic market valuation of wind probabilistic forecasts.
What_Worth_Learning: Precision in market formulations; avoiding conflation between cashflow and true forecast quality; exact pinball loss-to-quantile connection.

How_Novelty_Positioned: End-to-end decision-focused forecasting tailored to electricity trading.
What_Worth_Learning: Direct empirical precedent showing that minimizing MSE can actively degrade downstream economic value.

Title: Leakage and the reproducibility crisis in machine-learning-based science
Research_Question: How widespread is data leakage in scientific machine learning, and how does it systematically inflate reported performance?
Main_Contribution: Audits 329 papers across 17 scientific fields, identifying data leakage in dozens of subfields leading to unreproducible claims.
Dataset_Scale: 329 scientific papers across 17 disciplines.
Experimental_Design: Systematic scoping taxonomy categorizing train-test leakage, feature leakage, and preprocessing leakage.
Operational_Metric: Prevalence of leakage types, reported performance drop upon leakage correction.
Introduction_Structure: Reproducibility crisis in science -> ML adoption boom -> taxonomy of data leakage failure modes.
Contribution_Paragraph_Structure: Bullet breakdown of taxonomic survey, field-wide audit findings, and model debugging protocols.
Result_Section_Organization: Prevalence across disciplines -> taxonomy of failure modes -> re-implementation case studies.
Discussion_Style: Rigorous metascience critique, diagnosing incentive structures that favor unverified performance claims.
Limitation_Style: Acknowledges that paper text alone cannot detect all subtle forms of leakage without source code.
Table_Design: Clean cross-disciplinary audit matrix with clear counts, percentages, and failure categories.
Figure_Design: Taxonomic tree of leakage mechanisms; distribution bar charts across disciplines.
Claim_Strength: Level 1 & 2 (systematic empirical literature audit and verified re-implementation drops).
How_Causal_Language_Controlled: Scopes findings strictly to audited cohort; uses verified drops in re-implemented cases.
How_Novelty_Positioned: First comprehensive multi-disciplinary audit of leakage in ML-based science.
What_Worth_Learning: Exemplary metascience scoping audit structure; clear separation between audited cohort and broad domain.

Title: REFORMS: Consensus checklist for machine learning–based science
Research_Question: What reporting standards are required to ensure transparency, reproducibility, and rigorous evaluation in scientific ML?
Main_Contribution: Consensus 32-item checklist covering study design, data hygiene, model architecture, baseline parity, and negative controls.
Dataset_Scale: Consensus developed across 19 global experts across computer science, medicine, statistics, and engineering.
Experimental_Design: Delphi-style consensus procedure and systematic survey of reporting deficits.
Operational_Metric: Compliance rate across 32 disclosure items.
Introduction_Structure: ML opportunities in science -> reproducibility failures -> need for consensus checklist.
Contribution_Paragraph_Structure: Direct presentation of the 32-item REFORMS standard spanning five research lifecycle modules.
Result_Section_Organization: Module-by-module requirements: study goals -> data -> modeling -> evaluation -> transparency.
Discussion_Style: Normative, authoritative, establishing minimal disclosure requirements for top journals.
Limitation_Style: Emphasizes that checklists guide transparency but cannot replace rigorous experimental designs.
Table_Design: Structured 32-item checklist table with module grouping, item descriptors, and verification criteria.
Figure_Design: Lifecycle workflow diagram showing checkpoints from problem formulation to public release.
Claim_Strength: Level 2 (normative consensus guidelines and verified reporting practices).
How_Causal_Language_Controlled: Disciplined, professional, prescriptive without hyperbole.
How_Novelty_Positioned: First cross-disciplinary consensus checklist endorsed by Science.
What_Worth_Learning: Direct anchor paper for our reporting recommendations; formatting of audit checklists and baseline matching protocols.

Title: Reproducibility in machine learning for health research: Still a ways to go
Research_Question: To what extent do published machine learning healthcare studies adhere to reproducibility standards?
Main_Contribution: Audits 511 papers across code release, data availability, multiple-seed reporting, and baseline fairness.
Dataset_Scale: 511 peer-reviewed papers (2015-2020).
Experimental_Design: PRISMA scoping review with multi-rater double-blind coding across four reproducibility criteria.
Operational_Metric: Code availability rate (%), data access rate (%), multi-seed variance reporting rate (%).
Introduction_Structure: Clinical AI promise -> high-profile failures -> scoping audit protocol -> results overview.
Contribution_Paragraph_Structure: Structured summary of cohort size, extraction criteria, and four headline deficit statistics.
Result_Section_Organization: Overall reproducibility rates -> temporal trends (2015-2020) -> subfield breakdown -> code audit.
Discussion_Style: Constructive yet uncompromising assessment of field-wide transparency deficits.
Limitation_Style: Acknowledges proprietary patient privacy constraints on data release.
Table_Design: Clean tables with counts, percentages, and 95% confidence intervals across cohorts.
Figure_Design: Bar charts with Wilson confidence intervals; temporal compliance trend lines.

How_Causal_Language_Controlled: Every single numerical claim is tied strictly to audited cohort (e.g. "In our sample of 511 papers, only X%").
How_Novelty_Positioned: Largest empirical reproducibility audit of machine learning in medicine.
What_Worth_Learning: Gold standard exemplar for scoping review reporting: count + percentage primary, CI secondary, zero overclaiming.

Title: Deep reinforcement learning that matters
Journal: AAAI Conference on Human Computation and Work / AAAI
Research_Question: How do random seed selection, hyperparameter tuning, and code implementation differences confound empirical performance claims in deep RL?
Main_Contribution: Demonstrates that apparent algorithm improvements can be entirely artifacts of random seed cherry-picking and software library differences.
Dataset_Scale: OpenAI Gym benchmarks (MuJoCo, Atari) across 10+ random seeds and 5 distinct codebases.
Experimental_Design: Matched-capacity ablation varying exclusively random seeds, code implementations, and evaluation protocols.
Operational_Metric: Cumulative reward, policy variance across seeds, significance bootstrap intervals.
Introduction_Structure: RL breakthrough claims -> reproducibility concerns -> controlled stress-testing methodology.
Contribution_Paragraph_Structure: Clear 4-point summary isolating seed variance, baseline tuning, network architecture, and code divergence.
Result_Section_Organization: Seed variance demonstration -> codebase discrepancy audit -> statistical significance pitfalls.
Discussion_Style: Direct, forensic empirical exposure of methodological vulnerabilities in mainstream literature.
Limitation_Style: Emphasizes that deep RL remains promising but requires statistical discipline and open code.
Table_Design: Comparative matrix of identical algorithms across different public GitHub repositories showing divergent results.
Figure_Design: Multi-seed learning curves with individual seed trajectories illustrating extreme divergence.
Claim_Strength: Level 1 & 2 (forensic empirical demonstrations on benchmark environments).
How_Causal_Language_Controlled: Restrains claims to tested environments and codebases; demonstrates failure modes without universal condemnation.
How_Novelty_Positioned: Pioneering negative control and empirical audit paper in deep learning.
What_Worth_Learning: Structuring empirical audits with negative controls; showing software implementation divergence.

Title: Troubling trends in machine learning scholarship
Research_Question: What systematic methodological and rhetorical flaws undermine contemporary machine learning scholarship?
Main_Contribution: Identifies four troubling trends: failure to distinguish explanation from speculation, failure to identify empirical gains, mathiness, and misuse of language.
Dataset_Scale: Contemporary literature survey across top ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR).
Experimental_Design: Critical methodological synthesis and case study analysis.
Operational_Metric: Qualitative methodological rigor and argument validity.
Introduction_Structure: ML boom -> peer review strain -> four diagnostic patterns.
Contribution_Paragraph_Structure: Definition of four distinct methodological failures with specific diagnostic criteria.
Result_Section_Organization: Section 1: Speculation vs explanation; Section 2: Failure to identify gains; Section 3: Mathiness; Section 4: Language misuse.
Discussion_Style: Crisp, witty, rigorous analytical prose directly identifying bad academic habits.
Limitation_Style: Constructive guidelines for authors, reviewers, and program chairs.
Table_Design: None (essay / perspective).
Figure_Design: None.
Claim_Strength: Level 2 (supported epistemological analysis).
How_Causal_Language_Controlled: Directly critiques authors who conflate loose association or intuition with causal mechanisms.
How_Novelty_Positioned: Widely influential critical perspective (Lipton & Steinhardt).
What_Worth_Learning: Direct inspiration for our critique of mathiness and confounded module ablations; avoiding speculative explanations.

Title: Improving reproducibility in machine learning research
Research_Question: How can institutional conference programs and submission checklists increase code sharing, data transparency, and experimental rigor?
Main_Contribution: Reports the empirical impact of the NeurIPS Reproducibility Program across code submission rates, checklist adoption, and community response.
Dataset_Scale: Over 9,000 conference submissions to NeurIPS 2019 and 2020.
Experimental_Design: Multi-year observational cohort study tracking policy interventions.
Operational_Metric: Code submission proportion (%), compliance rate on error bars, hyperparameter specification rates.
Market_Formulation: Academic peer review and publication standards.
Introduction_Structure: The reproducibility crisis -> institutional interventions -> NeurIPS checklist rollout.
Contribution_Paragraph_Structure: Summary of checklist deployment, code submission trends, and community survey findings.
Result_Section_Organization: Checklist compliance metrics -> code availability progression -> author feedback analysis.
Discussion_Style: Empirical, institutional, data-grounded policy evaluation.
Limitation_Style: Notes that self-reported checklist compliance does not guarantee execution fidelity.
Table_Design: Categorical compliance percentage tables contrasting pre- and post-intervention cohorts.
Figure_Design: Temporal bar charts showing rising code attachment percentages.
Claim_Strength: Level 1 (exact empirical registry data from conference submission management systems).
How_Causal_Language_Controlled: Reports observed shifts associated with checklist introduction without claiming total culture transformation.
How_Novelty_Positioned: First large-scale institutional evaluation of reproducibility interventions in computer science.
What_Worth_Learning: Realistic reporting of checklist adoption; distinguishing between self-reported compliance and computational verification.

Title: Machine learning for science: Methodological failures and recommendations
Research_Question: What recurring methodological mistakes lead ML models to appear successful in benchmarks but fail upon real scientific deployment?
Main_Contribution: Identifies distribution shift, metric misalignment, circular evaluation, and baseline deflation as core failure mechanisms in science ML.
Dataset_Scale: Comprehensive review of applications across biology, climate, physics, and materials.
Experimental_Design: Diagnostic failure-mode taxonomy with concrete case studies.
Operational_Metric: Out-of-distribution generalization degradation, baseline parity gaps.
Introduction_Structure: ML adoption in natural sciences -> benchmark success vs deployment failure paradox -> core causes.
Contribution_Paragraph_Structure: Exposition of five critical traps with rigorous diagnostic checklists for peer reviewers.
Result_Section_Organization: Trap 1: Metric gaming; Trap 2: Baseline deflation; Trap 3: Distribution shifts; Trap 4: Circular validation.
Discussion_Style: Pragmatic, expert guidance for scientific reviewers and domain researchers.
Limitation_Style: Recognizes that obtaining truly independent out-of-distribution test sets is difficult in observational sciences.
Table_Design: Diagnostic rubric table mapping scientific traps to warning signs and corrective actions.
Figure_Design: Conceptual illustration of dataset leakage and distribution shift geometries.
Claim_Strength: Level 2 (epistemic and methodological synthesis).
How_Causal_Language_Controlled: Focuses on methodological identification rather than speculative assertions.
How_Novelty_Positioned: Landmark guidance paper for AI for Science evaluation.
What_Worth_Learning: Direct methodological guidance on how to spot deflated baselines and circular validation in scientific forecasting.

Title: Closing the AI accountability gap: The role of internal and external algorithmic audits
Journal: ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT)
Research_Question: How can structured multi-stage auditing protocols hold algorithm developers accountable throughout the model lifecycle?
Main_Contribution: Formulates the Algorithmic Audit Lifecycle (SMAATR) separating development stages: Scoping, Mapping, Artifact Collection, Testing, and Reporting.

Experimental_Design: Framework formulation and multi-stage lifecycle auditing trials.
Operational_Metric: Audit coverage, trace documentation completeness, failure mode detection rate.
Introduction_Structure: Accountability gap in deployed algorithms -> limitations of post-hoc explainability -> lifecycle audit proposal.
Contribution_Paragraph_Structure: Detailed definition of audit stages from scoping through artifact evaluation.
Result_Section_Organization: Phase-by-phase auditing protocol -> case study implementation -> governance recommendations.
Discussion_Style: Institutional, regulatory, and auditing metrology.
Limitation_Style: Notes trade-offs between proprietary confidentiality and public accountability.
Table_Design: Audit checklist tables mapping lifecycle phases to required verification artifacts.
Figure_Design: Lifecycle governance loop showing continuous auditing feedback.
Claim_Strength: Level 2 & 3 (rigorous auditing governance framework).
How_Causal_Language_Controlled: Defines formal auditing procedures rather than making unverified performance assertions.
How_Novelty_Positioned: Foundational paper defining algorithmic auditing methodologies.
